reflection: Round 1 with an empty notebook, so there is no evidence yet. I will try a mix of mean-reversion, volatility-regime and cross-asset ideas. The existing top factors are AAPL vol and MSFT 1d return, so I build on those. The improve and partner slots have no parents in the notebook, so I fill them with variants of the existing useful factors, treated as parents. I will watch which years and which models (LR vs RF) respond.

factors.name: aapl_vol_ratio_5_20
factors.hypothesis: The raw vol level is regime-dependent across years (2022 and 2025 high vol). Normalising short vol by long-run vol gives a stationary vol-expansion signal.

factors.name: msft_return_zscore_20
factors.hypothesis: MSFT's 1d return matters but its scale shifts with regimes. Standardising by recent vol makes the shock comparable across years.

factors.name: aapl_close_zscore_60
factors.hypothesis: Position of Apple's price within its 60-day distribution captures longer mean-reversion or trend that the 20-day factors miss.

factors.name: qqq_vol_ratio_5_60
factors.hypothesis: Sector-wide vol expansion relative to normal indicates stress, after which next-day rebounds are more likely.

factors.name: aapl_overnight_gap
factors.hypothesis: Apple's overnight gap relative to QQQ's gap, taken in a vol context, shows idiosyncratic news that may partly revert or continue.

factors.name: aapl_close_location_minus_qqq
factors.formula: subtract(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Close, AAPL_Low), subtract(AAPL_High, AAPL_Low)), safe_divide(subtract(QQQ_Close, QQQ_Low), subtract(QQQ_High, QQQ_Low)))
factors.hypothesis: Where Apple closed in its daily range versus where QQQ closed, as a complement to the MSFT move, shows late-day relative strength or weakness.
